claims.statement: The `/security/[security_id]` server load validates the param and returns only `{ security_id }` — it deliberately does not await the security identity or its price series, throwing `error(400, 'Security ID is required')` when the param is missing.

`SecurityPageDataService.load(securityId)` fetches the security identity and its `1d` price series in parallel via `Promise.all`, guards against stale responses with a `loadSeq` counter, never throws (returning the caught error instead), treats an empty price series as a successful load whose message lands in `error`, and only the newest sequence clears `isLoading`.

The security page's mount `$effect` keyed on `data.security_id` owns the post-navigation init: it returns early when `data.security_id !== securityId`, routes a load error through `redirectOn401`, loads preferences once, maps the `1d` items to candles, runs `loadAlerts()` / `loadHoldings()` / `drawingsService.loadSnapshots()` in parallel, gates the wave-alert reconcile on `userPreferences !== null`, and dynamically imports `security-chart.svelte` only after data exists.

The security page titlebar renders instantly by resolving the security from `watchlistService.defaultWatchlistSecurities` as `instantSecurity` and preferring `pageData.security ?? instantSecurity`, so shortcut navigation renders identity before the fetch lands while a direct URL load falls back to the header skeleton.

The security page renders six actions-sidebar groups in a fixed order, each expanded: HoldingsGroup, IndicatorsGroup, PriceAlertsGroup, NotesGroup, DocumentsGroup and AIAnalysisGroup; holdings/indicators/alerts receive page-owned state while notes, documents and AI receive only `securityId`.

The sidebar groups share two primitives: `GroupTitle`, which renders a collapsible `Sidebar.GroupLabel` button with a rotating chevron plus an optional `Sidebar.GroupAction` icon button carrying `actionTitle` as its aria-label/title, and `SidebarError`, which renders a message and an optional 'Try again' retry button.

The implemented actions sidebar covers only part of the OpenSpec requirements in `openspec/specs/actions-sidebar/spec.md`: the header/expand/collapse contract, the group action button and action-item hover/focus states exist, but there are no group dividers, badges, mobile drawer mode, and the groups are not collapsed by default because every call site passes `expanded={true}`.

Notes and documents groups treat an HTTP 404 from their list fetch as an empty list rather than an error, assigning `[]` and only routing other statuses into the `SidebarError` message; both groups re-fetch after a successful create/update/delete instead of patching local state.

The note write path is title-less from the client: `SecurityNoteCreateRequest` and `SecurityNoteUpdateRequest` carry only `content`, the note list item falls back to a 100-character content preview when `title` is absent, and the backend enqueues `generate_note_title_task(note_id, request_id=get_request_id())` after both the create and the update (the server update is a PUT while the frontend client calls `this.patch`).

`generate_note_title_task` seeds the request id and runs `_generate_note_title`, which returns immediately when `huey.svcs_registry` is `None`, opens its own svcs Container, returns silently when the note is not found, calls `ai_service.generate_note_title(note.content)`, and writes the result back through the title-only `note_repository.update_title(note_id, title)`.

`AIService.generate_note_title` calls chat completions with `model="gpt-4-turbo"`, `temperature=0.3`, `max_tokens=20` and `timeout=10`, strips surrounding quotes, truncates to `MAX_TITLE_LENGTH = 50`, and on any exception logs the failure and returns the note content truncated to 47 characters plus an ellipsis (or the content unchanged), so a provider outage never leaves the title unset.

`StubAIService` implements only `analyze_fundamentals`, `summarize_notes` and `analyze_portfolio_fit` — it has no `generate_note_title` — so stub or test environments cannot run the title task through the stub; `tests/routers/test_notes.py` instead patches `src.market.task.Container` with a mock returning an `AsyncMock(spec=AIService)` and invokes `_generate_note_title` directly.

`GET /market/securities/{security_id}/notes` returns a `PaginatedResponse[SecurityNoteRead]` driven by the shared `PaginationParams`, with the repository defaulting to `offset=0, limit=50` ordering by `created_at.desc()`; the sidebar consumes only `res.items` and has no pagination control.

`DocumentUploadDialog` validates allowed types (`application/pdf`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg`, `text/plain`) and a 10 MB (`10 * 1024 * 1024`) size cap client-side, setting a type or size error and clearing the selection on rejection; this differs from the `security-documents` OpenSpec list of PDF/DOC/DOCX/TXT, and the spec's upload progress and filename filter are not implemented.

`POST /market/securities/{security_id}/documents` resolves the storage directory from `settings.upload_path` (default `data/uploads`), writes the file under a random `f"{uuid.uuid4()}{file_ext}"` name, records `file_size` from the in-memory body read, and persists the original `filename` with the client-declared `content_type` (falling back to `application/octet-stream`) — there is no magic-byte sniffing or server-side size cap.

`GET /market/securities/{security_id}/documents` returns a plain list (not a paginated envelope) ordered `created_at.desc()` for the calling user, which is why the frontend `getDocuments` returns `SecurityDocument[]` while notes and alerts return `PaginatedResponse<T>`.

There is frontend/backend drift on document download: `frontend/src/lib/api/documentsService.ts` targets `GET /market/securities/{security_id}/documents/{doc_id}/download`, but `src/market/router.py` exposes only GET (list), POST (upload) and DELETE for documents — no download route exists anywhere in the backend and `tests/routers/test_documents.py` covers only upload and list, so the download button, image/PDF preview and `file_path` client-side have no server endpoint.

`accountService.getHoldings(securityId)` targets `GET /accounts/holdings/{security_id}` in the account domain, returning `PaginatedResponse[AccountHoldingRead]` with `account_id`, `account_name`, `quantity`, optional `average_cost`, `total_value`, `currency` and optional `account_total_value` / `account_percentage`.

`PositionService.get_holdings_by_security` returns `([], 0)` when the security is not found, then computes `holding_total_value = quantity * latest_price` from `MarketPricesApi.get_latest_close`, labels holdings with the security currency, and derives `account_percentage` only when the account total is positive, converting the holding value into the account currency first; the repository row supplies `total_value=0.0` and `currency=""` marked as populated by the service layer.

`HoldingGroup.fetchHoldings` fans out `accountService.getHoldings(securityId)`, `accountClient.getAccounts()` and one `accountClient.getAccountTotals(acc.id)` per account, then computes `portfolioPercentage` as the security's summed `total_value` over the sum of per-account totals (or 0 when the portfolio total is not positive); any failure sets 'Failed to load holdings' and renders `SidebarError` with `fetchHoldings` as retry.

`blendedAverageCost` is a quantity-weighted average that returns 0 for an empty list or zero total quantity and treats a missing `average_cost` as 0; it is consumed twice on the security page — by the sidebar's 'Average' line and, independently, by the page's own `loadHoldings()` which feeds the chart's `avgPrice` dashed line via `averagePrice`/`showAveragePrice`.

The security page owns the `alerts` array because the chart draws price lines from it: `ChartComponent` receives `{alerts}`, `onAddAlert={handleCreateAlert}` and `onRemoveAlert={handleDeleteAlert}`, and all mutations are followed by a re-fetch; `PriceAlertsGroup` prefers the page-supplied bindable `alerts` and only self-fetches when it is absent.

Elliott-wave drawing reconciles price alerts automatically: `reconcileWaveAlertsForSecurity` diffs the desired levels computed from wave settings and drawn waves against the current alerts, deletes obsolete ones, creates missing ones with `source: 'wave'`, and reloads if anything changed; reconciles are serialized on a single promise chain because `onWaveChange` fires per point, are skipped while rewound, are gated on preferences having loaded, and swallow failures so drawing never breaks.

`AIAnalysisGroup` performs no fetch on mount; it renders three fixed actions ('Explain Fundamentals', 'Summarize Notes', 'Portfolio Debate') that open `AIResponseDialog` in a loading state and call the matching `aiService` method, with retry re-invoking the same action, and its Portfolio Debate action sends the placeholder `portfolio_context: 'Analyzing in isolation for now.'` rather than real holdings.

All sidebar dialogs use the shared `ModalState` helper for open/close and for carrying the subject (`ModalState<SecurityNote>`, `ModalState<SecurityDocument>`, `ModalState<number>` for a delete-confirm id), and the note creation and document upload dialogs bind 'primary action on Enter' via a keydown handler, with Shift+Enter reserved for a newline in the note textarea.

The security route's stale-response guards are load-bearing invariants: `loadSeq` in `SecurityPageDataService`, the `sequenceCounter`/`indicatorSeq`/`activeRefreshSeq` triplet for indicator computes, and the `data.security_id !== securityId` check in the mount effect each prevent a superseded navigation or toggle from overwriting newer state.
